newsitem.title: UK: KPMG posts rise in UK profits after outside audit.
newsitem.headline: KPMG posts rise in UK profits after outside audit.

text.p: Accounting firm KPMG International's UK arm on Monday released its first ever externally-audited accounts, posting increases in profits and fees for 1996.
KPMG UK said its pretax proprietorship profit jumped to 24.2 million stg in 1996 compared with 17.9 million stg in the previous year, while gross fees rose 6.0 percent to 623.5 million stg.
KPMG International's new chairman, Colin Sharman, said he expected the release of audited results to help attract clients and personnel to the firm's UK division.
"We believe that public and political opinion is moving towards full disclosure by professional firms and that we are right to provide this information," he told a news conference.

When asked whether the firm planned to release externally-audited results at its other divisions, Sharman said, "I think it's a little bit early to start talking about that. But I believe that this is the way forward."
Sharman, senior UK partner, took over as KPMG International chairman as of Saturday.
KPMG UK's results, audited by Grant Thornton, showed that audit and accounting fees grew 5.0 percent to 258 million stg last year, while corporate finance fees jumped 41 percent to 29 million stg.
Tax advisory revenues rose 9.0 percent to 130 million stg.
Management consulting fees fell 2.0 percent to 107 million stg, but Sharman said the division had recovered from weakness at the start of last year.

Management consulting fees rose 32 percent in the first quarter ended in December, while KPMG UK's earned income was up 15 percent and transaction services grew 35 percent in the quarter, Sharman said.
KPMG UK accounted for 17-18 percent of the group's total revenues of $8.1 billion in 1996, he said.
The division includes about 561 of KPMG International's total 6,250 partners.
